subject: Data capture & deletion: default retention for prompts/outputs and deletion playbook
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <security@brightbank.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Clarify what you retain by default (prompts, outputs, streaming)

Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this call earlier. A few follow-ups from BrightBank's security team so we can finish our internal risk assessment:

1) What does Redwood keep by default for hosted API calls? Specifically: raw prompts, model-generated outputs, streaming fragments, KV cache entries, and embeddings.

2) How long are these individual artifacts retained? We need precise default windows and whether those are adjustable for enterprise customers.

3) If we request a full deletion for a given account and time range, what is the expected timeline and what artifacts can you guarantee removal of? Do you delete cached / deduplicated derivatives as well?

4) For streaming responses (prefix fragments and partial tokens), are fragments ever persisted beyond transient buffers?

Appreciate a short, bulletized response we can include in our compliance package. If possible please attach your SOC2 snapshot and a short deletion playbook.

Thanks —
Lena Ortiz

Subject: Re: Clarify what you retain by default (prompts, outputs, streaming)

Hi Lena —

Below is a concise breakdown you can place in your package. I'll keep this focused on default hosted-policy behavior; I'll add notes on enterprise overrides at the end.

Summary (hosted API defaults — Redwood-managed):
- Raw request payloads (prompts including user messages): retained for 30 days by default. These are used for troubleshooting and rate-limiting forensic checks.
- Model-generated outputs (finalized responses sent to customers): retained for 90 days by default for quality monitoring and regression detection.
- Streaming fragments / partial tokens: not persisted to long-term storage by default. Streaming chunks live in transit and short-lived buffers; persisted snapshots of a streaming session are only kept if the request completes and becomes part of the stored request/response pair.
- KV cache / session caches (in-memory + short-term disk caches used to accelerate inference): ephemeral; cache tombstones and metadata are rotated within 48 hours in normal operation. Persistent KV snapshots are not kept unless explicitly enabled by the customer (e.g., for session continuity features).
- Embeddings and vector artifacts created via the embeddings endpoint: retained for 365 days by default to support similarity indexing and product features.
- Aggregated telemetry (latency histograms, token counts, anonymized error rates): retained for 2 years for analytics and SLO reporting; this data is aggregated and cannot be tied to a specific prompt or PII without additional logs.

Enterprise/private variations (common patterns):
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity customers can request reduced retention windows contractually (e.g., 7/30/90 -> 0/30/7 depending on profile).
- Private/on-prem deployments: Redwood does not control retention; the customer/operator configures retention in the deployment manifest.

Deletion guarantees & practical playbook:
1) Scope of deletions: we can delete stored requests, stored outputs, persisted embeddings and associated indices for a given account and time range. We also remove corresponding diagnostic logs that directly reference request IDs.
2) Derivatives & deduplicated data: derivatives that were materialized and indexed (for example, an embedding that was persisted into a shared index) will be removed from the account-scoped indices; however, if a derivative was aggregated into anonymized telemetry or model improvement datasets in a way that strip identifiers, we cannot retroactively remove it from already-aggregated, anonymized analytics.
3) Timeline: standard hosted deletion workflow target is 5 business days after validated request; complex cases (cross-region, historical backfills) may take up to 15 business days. We provide a deletion report (IDs removed, stores touched) when complete.
4) Self-service & API: Customers can submit a deletion request via our portal (hubspot ticket auto-generated) and include either (a) request IDs, (b) time range + API key, or (c) account id + date range to scope deletions. For BrightBank we recommend including the account id and the range to avoid gaps.
5) Verification & audit: We produce a deletion manifest and an engineer-signed audit note for SOC/compliance review. For enterprise customers we can also provide an on-prem runbook and screen-sharing to demonstrate deletion steps.

Operational notes for support engineers (internal runbook extract):
- Step 1: Confirm identity & authorization on HubSpot ticket (link provided).
- Step 2: Validate account ID and time range; request a sample of 3 request IDs to confirm scope.
- Step 3: Run deletion job: delete-requests --account=BRIGHTBANK --from=2026-01-01 --to=2026-06-30 --dry-run=false
- Step 4: Purge embeddings: remove-embeddings --account=BRIGHTBANK --index=brightbank-prod-vec --confirm
- Step 5: Remove related diagnostic logs: diagnostics-prune --account=BRIGHTBANK --cutoff=2026-06-30
- Step 6: Produce Deletion Report (CSV) and upload to drive; attach to HubSpot ticket.

Notes on streaming & KV cache edge cases:
- If a streaming session was interrupted and only partial fragments were materialized into the request log, those fragments are subject to the normal request retention window (30 days) unless the account requests an immediate purge.
- KV cache entries used solely for ephemeral acceleration are not included in long-term retention; however tombstone/metadata artifacts may exist for short windows and will be purged per the cache rotation schedule.

Please let us know if you want us to reduce the default windows for BrightBank under a Dedicated or Private arrangement — we can include that language in the SOW.

-Karthik
